answers.explanation: The server let a stranger request AXFR. Restrict it to your secondaries.
Someone spoofed the victim's address in small queries to open resolvers.
One poisoned cache, many victims, until the TTL ran out.
The forged answer couldn't carry a valid signature from bank.com's key.
Stolen data, encoded in the names, smuggled out through allowed DNS traffic.
Whoever controls the NS records controls every name in the domain. Registrar accounts need MFA and a registry lock.
Only encryption hides the queries. DNSSEC would prove the answers are genuine but leave them visible.
Registering look-alike names and waiting for mistakes.
